interactions.summary: A student reads Justinian's self-introduction from Paradise VI, including his conversion under Agapetus and his trust in Belisarius, before Jiang pauses to supply the historical background.
Jiang explains that Justinian rules the Byzantine or Eastern Roman Empire after Rome's split, then describes his campaign to reunify the empire and impose Trinitarian Christianity through Belisarius.
The student continues Justinian's survey of Rome from Alba Longa through the early republic, and Jiang glosses it as a compressed summary of Roman origins from the Sabine women to Lucretia's suicide.

speaker_notes.note: These focus refs are quoted Dante read aloud by a student, not Jiang's own prose.

claims.claim: The student reading presents Justinian as the emperor who purged vain laws, was corrected by Pope Agapetus on Christ's two natures, and delegated military action to Belisarius.
Jiang says Justinian rules the Byzantine or Eastern Roman Empire after the Roman world splits into eastern and western halves.

Jiang says the imperial split produces competing Christian variants, many of which reject the Holy Trinity, and he frames Justinian's campaigns as an attempt to reunify the empire and enforce Trinitarian orthodoxy.
Jiang identifies Belisarius as Justinian's general during this imperial reconquest.
The canto's next movement, as read aloud by the student, shifts from Justinian's self-account to a rapid survey of Rome's rise under the imperial eagle.
Jiang glosses the references to the Sabine women and Lucretia as part of a compressed recap of the Roman Republic's early history before empire.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang compresses late antique theology and geopolitics into one stark picture: Justinian wages holy war to reunify Rome and impose the Trinity.
signature_moments.source_phrase: this Holy Crusade to conquer and unite all the Roman Empire and enforce the Holy Trinity
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It turns the canto's dense historical frame into a legible model of empire as theological enforcement.

signature_moments.moment: The Roman eagle begins its world-historical sweep, and Jiang reduces a thicket of names into the founding grammar of republic becoming empire.
signature_moments.source_phrase: summarizing the history of the Roman Republic which then gives birth to the Roman Empire
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the lecture's pivot from Justinian's biography to Rome's providential storyline.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The Byzantine general Jiang names as Justinian's military instrument in the reconquest of the Roman world.
The orthodox doctrine Jiang says Justinian sought to impose across a divided Christian empire.
A marker from early Roman history Jiang uses to orient the canto's compressed review of the Roman Republic.

chronology_notes.note: Jiang frames Paradise VI as a long chronology: first the split Roman Empire under Justinian, then a compressed return to Rome's pre-imperial origins.
